subdomain: 3.3 Evaluate accuracy-latency trade-offs and justify configuration decisions

en.question: A document-comparison service requires at least 98% task accuracy and p95 end-to-end completion latency no greater than 6 seconds. On the same representative test set, configuration A achieves 99.2% and 8.1 seconds, B achieves 97.4% and 4.3 seconds, C achieves 98.6% and 5.8 seconds, and D achieves 98.9% and 6.7 seconds. Which configuration meets both stated gates?

options.text: Configuration C, because its measured accuracy and p95 completion time both satisfy the requirements.
options.note: Its 98.6% task accuracy exceeds the 98% minimum and its 5.8-second p95 is below the 6-second ceiling. No trade-off against either acceptance gate is needed.

options.text: Configuration A, because the highest task accuracy should take precedence over the latency ceiling.
options.note: Its 8.1-second p95 violates the explicit latency requirement. Higher accuracy does not authorize ignoring a separate mandatory service-level gate.

options.text: Configuration B, because the fastest p95 compensates for its slightly lower task accuracy.
options.note: Its 97.4% task accuracy is below the required 98%. The requirements are independent gates rather than a score in which speed can offset incorrect answers.

options.text: Configuration D, because a p95 over the limit can be accepted if the median is likely to be lower.
options.note: The stated requirement concerns p95, not an inferred median. Its 6.7-second p95 fails that requirement even if most individual requests are faster.
